name: Hardware-accelerated surface voxelization via 2D textures
definition: A technique that transfers intersection computation from geometric space to image space by rasterizing model surfaces into 2D textures, allowing collision detection and volumetric rendering at real-time frame rates.
summary: Hardware-accelerated surface voxelization via 2D textures rasterizes models into 2D textures for real-time volumetric rendering, differing from slicing-based methods by being view-independent and performance-insensitive to scene complexity.
